sections.text: Introduction

Horizontal and
 outboard movements may involve walking across a tower arm or the bridge or a
 shaft of the tower. These movements may also involve the use of suspension
 platforms, rope Ladders. This Procedure outlines some of the options that may
 be used for temporary fall protection during these movements to access the
 work location on the tower.
Safety Precautions

 your safety Belts

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

Horizontal Movement on the Tower - Double Belting
System

items:
The double belting
 system which is comprised of a shock absorbing lanyard and pole strapis the
 most common fall protection system used when making horizontal movements on
 towers.

Attach a shock
 absorbing lanyard to the back D ring of the harness and then connecta
 large karabiner to the other end of the lanyard.

Move horizontally out
 the arm or across the tower bridge or shaft by alternately relocating the
 karabiner and the pole strap to provide continuous attachment to the tower
 members See Fig 1.

sections.text: Figure 1 Using a Double Belting System
Retractable Lanyard

items:
Install a nylon sling on a cross member of the tower shaft
 or leg of the structure.

Connect the retractable lanyard housing to the sling to
 allow the line to be fed out 
 vertically.

Connect the retractable lanyard housing to the sling to
 allow the line to be fed out 
 vertically.

Thread the line through a large karabiner or sling on the
 leg or a member below the housing to change the direction of the line form
 vertical to horizontal. See Fig 2.

Attach the end of the lanyard to a shock absorber on the
 back D of the body harness.

Install Karabiners over the line and attach them to the
 members as you move along to minimize any pendulum motion if you should
 slip. Inserting the line through karabiners will also prevent the lanyard
 from excessive rubbing on the steel members as you walk across the arm.

This system is useful when moving across bridge sections and tower arms
 when descending to de-energized conductor levels on a rope ladder.

Method of Attaching the Retractable Lanyard to the Tower
When moving along the arm

Rope Anchored above the Walkway
Location

items:
Belt in to the tower
 leg or ladder at the height location where horizontal movement towards the
 end of the arm will begin.

Attach a 16 mm(5/8 in)
 nylon rope to the back side of an anchor hook and then install the hook with
 the switch sticks to a suitable location above the path of horizontal
 movement. Choose a location to minimize pendulum motion in the event of a
 slip.
 Note: If
 there is a possibility that the nylon rope could encroach on the limit of
 approach to live conductors, substitute an approved live-line rope for the
 nylon rope.

Where possible, use
 the main horizontal members of the arm above the anchor point.

Install the fall
 arrester onto the rope in such a way as to minimize slack but still allow
 movement

out of the arm. See
 Fig 3.

Un belt from the tower
 steel or ladder and proceed to move horizontally along the tower arm.

Belt to an arm member when the
 anchor hook must be relocated.

sections.text:
Figure 3:
Using a Rope Anchored above the Walkway
Temporary Restraint Rope

items:
A temporary
 restraint rope may be installed along the arm or across the bridge when many
 trips are required to the work location.

Tie one end of 16mm
 (5/8 in) nylon rope to a sling or karabiner installed near the end of the
 tower or bridge.

String the rope
 through karabiners or nylon slings that have been installed 3 m to 4.5m (10
 to 15 ft) apart across the arm or bridge. The karabiners or slings should be
 installed at a convenient height so that the shock absorber from the body
 harness can be attached to the rope that is strung through them.

Tie the other end
 of the rope to the shaft or other end of the bridge or string it across to
 the other arm when required .See Fig 4.

Attach a karabiner to the shock absorber on the back
 D of the body harness.

Connect the karabiner to the rope when moving
 horizontally across the arm.

Belt to a tower member when relocating the karabiner
 around the members or the karabiners holding the rope.

Only one person at a time may use the rope for fall protection. Other
 persons line maintainers must be belted to the tower members when the rope
 is in use.

sections.text:
Figure 4:
Using a Temporary Restraint Rope
Outboard Movement On The Tower
Retractable Lanyard

items:
Connect the retractable lanyard housing to the tower and
 move along the arm in the same manner as outlined in Section 3.2.

When a suspension platform is required for access, install a
 sling and karabiner at the end of the arm and feed the lanyard through the
 karabiner before proceeding out on the platform. See Figure 5.

By changing the direction with a karabiner, the retractable lanyard can
 also be used when descending to the de-energized conductor level on a rope
 ladder.

sections.text:
Figure 5:
Using a retractable Lanyard When accessing the Work Location on a Suspension Platform

Rope Anchored above the Work
Location

items:
Install the anchor hook and rope in a similar manner to the
 method outlined in last section

Now, un belt from the tower member and proceed to the work
 location, allowing the fall arrester to move along the rope.

Lock the fall arrester onto the rope, at the work location
 to minimize the fall distance.
Reverse this sequence when proceeding back to the arm.

Another method of using a rope for outboard fall protection,
 is to have a second ok attach a rope to the next tower arm or shield wire
 peak above the work location. The transmission line maintainer below can
 attach himself to the rope and proceed outboard to the work location. Slack
 should be kept out of the rope to minimize pendulum motion should a slip
 occur.

sections.text: Safety Summary

The following hazards and precautions are emphasized to
highlight some of the safety considerations related to using temporary fall
protection systems on a tower. Other hazards which are site specific or of a
general nature must be identified during the tailboard conference before the
work begins.

rows: - Minimize the slack in all fall protection systems.

-
 Observe the limits of approach when using fall protection systems.
- Inspect all fall protection equipment before use.
- Replace any component in the system that has arrested a fall.
- Always have a full structure length rope or hand line available
as well as karabiners for possible rescue at the work location.
